ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A flowerpot accidentally falls from the 10th floor (approximately $h=30\mathrm{m}$ above the ground) windowsill. Neglecting air resistance (simplifying the motion of the flowerpot to free fall), the mass of the flowerpot is $m=2\mathrm{kg}$, and the gravitational acceleration $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. During the process of the flowerpot falling to the ground, the work done by gravity on the flowerpot $W$
2. The instantaneous power of gravity at the end of 2 seconds when the flowerpot falls.
3. The average power of gravity during the 2nd second of the flowerpot's fall

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Given free fall from rest with height h = 30 m, mass m = 2 kg, and gravitational acceleration g = 10 m/s^2. The gravitational force is F = mg = 2 × 10 = 20 N. 1. Work done by gravity over the full fall: W = Fh = mgh = 2 × 10 × 30 = 600 J. 2. Instantaneous power at t = 2 s: the speed after 2 seconds is v = gt = 10 × 2 = 20 m/s. Power is P = Fv = mgv = 20 × 20 = 400 W. 3. Average power during the 2nd second means from t = 1 s to t = 2 s. The displacement fallen by time t is s = (1/2)gt^2. Thus s(2) = (1/2) × 10 × 2^2 = 20 m, and s(1) = (1/2) × 10 × 1^2 = 5 m. The distance during the 2nd second is Δs = 20 - 5 = 15 m. Work in that interval is ΔW = mgΔs = 20 × 15 = 300 J. Since Δt = 1 s, average power is P_avg = ΔW/Δt = 300/1 = 300 W.
